Mercer Intl posts Q3 net loss of $80.8M, embarks on recapitalization plan

VANCOUVER, British Columbia — Mercer International, a global forest products company, recorded a net loss of $59.2 million compared to net losses of $80.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 and $76.0 million in the second quarter of 2026.

The company reported total revenues for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by approximately 4% to $440.7 million from $458.1 million in the same period of 2025 primarily as a result of lower pulp sales volumes and realizations. The company said this decrease was partially offset by higher energy and solid wood products sales realizations.

Mercer’s solid wood segment revenues in the third quarter of 2026 increased by approximately 10% to $128.6 million from $117.2 million in the same period of 2025 as a result of higher revenue from all product categories except for pallets. Revenues for lumber, which accounted for 53% of the solid wood segment, increased approximately 11% to $68.0 million from $61.0.

Mercer announced November 2 that it entered into restructuring support agreements with holders of more than 87% of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of its senior notes and with holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of our common stock that provide for a comprehensive recapitalization of the company. The transaction provides for, among other things, the exchange of approximately $1.1 billion of existing senior notes for equity, eliminates approximately $96 million of annual cash interest on the copmany's notes and provides for $400 million of new capital through a fully-backstopped rights offering of senior secured notes. Mercer said the recapitalization is expected to significantly reduce its debt, extend its maturity runway and provide substantial new liquidity.

Juan Carlos Bueno, CEO of Mercer, commented on the recapitalization. “Market and industry-wide pressures continue to persist as we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, he said. “With the support of the majority of our noteholders and shareholders, we are putting in place a much stronger balance sheet. As we work to complete the recapitalization, our focus remains on business fundamentals, where cost reduction, operational efficiency, and cash flow preservation are key. We will also continue exploring opportunities for additional government support, where appropriate. The recapitalization is a key step in achieving necessary deleveraging to position us toward long-term stability and growth as market conditions improve in the future.”

Rich Christianson is the owner of Richson Media LLC, a Chicago-based communications firm focused on the industrial woodworking sector. Rich is the former long-time editorial director and associate publisher of Woodworking Network. During his nearly 35-year career, Rich has toured more than 250 woodworking operations throughout North America, Europe and Asia and has written extensively on woodworking technology, design and supply trends. He has also directed and promoted dozens of woodworking trade shows, conferences and seminars including the Cabinets & Closets Conference & Expo and the Woodworking Machinery & Supply Conference & Expo, Canada’s largest woodworking show.
